rubric.why: The student identifies the periodic recurrence of properties when elements are ordered by atomic number.
rubric.how: Award for stating that properties recur periodically when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: Similar outer-shell electron arrangements recur at regular intervals and account for the similar properties.
rubric.how: Award for linking the repetition to the recurrence of similar outer-shell electron configurations.

modelAnswer: When elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, their properties recur after regular intervals.
This periodic repetition occurs because similar outer-shell electron configurations recur.

items.followUp: Explain why water molecules attract one another through dipole–dipole forces.

rubric.why: HCl is polar because chlorine attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen.
rubric.how: Award for identifying HCl as polar and relating this to the difference in electronegativity.

rubric.why: The oppositely charged ends of neighboring polar molecules attract.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the partial positive end of one molecule attracts the partial negative end of another.

modelAnswer: HCl is a polar molecule because chlorine attracts the shared electron pair more strongly than hydrogen.
The partial positive end of one HCl molecule attracts the partial negative end of another, producing dipole–dipole forces.

items.followUp: Write any two properties of gases.

rubric.how: Award for stating that a liquid has a definite volume.

accept: takes the shape of its container
rubric.why: Liquids do not have a fixed shape and take the shape of their container.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a liquid has no definite shape or takes the shape of its container.

modelAnswer: A liquid has a definite volume.
A liquid has no definite shape and takes the shape of its container.

items.followUp: Give two differences between a true solution and a colloid.

rubric.why: A solution is homogeneous, whereas a suspension is heterogeneous.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting a solution as homogeneous with a suspension as heterogeneous.

rubric.why: Suspension particles settle on standing and can be separated by filtration; solution particles do not settle and pass through ordinary filter paper.
rubric.how: Award for one correct contrast: suspension particles settle while solution particles do not, or suspensions can be filtered while solutions cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is homogeneous, while a suspension is heterogeneous.
Particles in a suspension settle on standing and can be separated by filtration; particles in a solution do not settle and pass through ordinary filter paper.

items.followUp: What is a saturated solution? How can it be made unsaturated?

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution contains less dissolved solute than the maximum amount possible at that temperature.
rubric.how: Award for defining it as containing less than the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a specified temperature.

rubric.why: Adding solute increases the amount dissolved until the solution reaches its saturation limit.
rubric.description: Changing it to a saturated solution
rubric.how: Award for stating that more solute is added until no more dissolves at that temperature.

modelAnswer: An unsaturated solution contains less solute than the maximum amount that can dissolve at a given temperature.
It can be changed into a saturated solution by adding more solute until no more dissolves at that temperature.

items.followUp: Define oxidation in terms of hydrogen and oxygen.

rubric.why: Reduction can be described as the gain of hydrogen or the removal of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award for stating that reduction is gain of hydrogen.

rubric.why: Reduction is also defined as removal of oxygen from a substance.
rubric.how: Award for stating that reduction is removal or loss of oxygen.

modelAnswer: Reduction is the gain of hydrogen by a substance.
Reduction is the removal of oxygen from a substance.

items.followUp: Calculate the oxidation number of sulphur in SO₃.

rubric.why: Sodium has oxidation number +1 and oxygen has oxidation number −2 in sodium sulfate.
rubric.how: Award for correctly assigning +1 to Na and −2 to O.

rubric.why: The oxidation numbers in a neutral formula unit sum to zero, giving sulphur an oxidation number of +6.
rubric.how: Award for the correct sulphur oxidation number, +6.

modelAnswer: Let the oxidation number of S be x: 2(+1) + x + 4(−2) = 0.

items.followUp: What compounds are formed when lithium and sodium react with oxygen?

rubric.why: Group I metals react with oxygen to form oxygen compounds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Group I metals combine with oxygen to form oxides or related oxygen compounds.

rubric.why: The characteristic products include lithium oxide, sodium peroxide and potassium superoxide.
rubric.how: Award for giving the correct Group I oxygen products, such as Li₂O, Na₂O₂ and KO₂.

modelAnswer: Group I metals react with oxygen to form oxides or related oxygen compounds.
Lithium forms Li₂O, sodium forms Na₂O₂, and potassium forms KO₂.
